title: Ask HN: Getting around NPM typo squatting?
summary:
Hey HN,

I feel like there are a lot of potential NPM package names out there that are being overzealously guarded against usage.

There's a package name that I want, for example, which 404s + does not exist. However, when I try to run `npm publish` with that name it gets rejected by NPM for being "too similar" to a laundry list of other packages which (in my opinion) aren't plausible typos.

I feel like the typo squatting system started in good faith -- i.e. to prevent someone from taking the `left-pad` or `leftpsd` name when `leftpad` already existed. Occasionally I'll come across packages that have a deprecation + NPM contact email[0] which nowadays just auto-rejects any email sent to it. You can't seem to get around this issue by talking to a human anymore -- understandably so due to the certain increase GitHub (owner of NPM now) in support spam from bots + LLMs. I just don't get any replies from support tickets I create.

There are also a lot of really neat package names which are almost certainly no longer used whatsoever. I contacted someone once about using a name they hadn't updated for a decade -- and they wanted at least $5k USD to hand it over.

I found an interesting article talking about this shift from only a month ago[1] -- but I'm curious what other people think about this and if anything has worked for you?

[0] - https://www.npmjs.com/package/solidify

[1] - https://smoores.dev/post/no_npm_estee_is_not_a_typo/

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50652314

title: I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the AI
summary:
A few years ago talking heads and AM radio personalities went cookoo over AI. The warnings were replete with assertations of total destruction. I blew them off as doomsdayesque viewer/listener headline/listener bastards that saw dollar signs in words.

Assuredly, they completely misunderstood the technology and the intricacies of how AI functions and what it was capable of. They read enough science fiction to regurgitate what sounded like knowledge of the future.

Interestingly, they were largely right in the end. The tech has evolved fantastically quick. The wildest scenarios preposed from previous predicions is becoming realistic.

I do not worry about those scenarios. I do not fear the wildest predictions. Throughout history humans have developed weapons, ideas, technologies, and systems that detractors predicted would kill us all or would lead to insurmountable changes to society.

Electricity is not the devil. The printing press was not a detriment to society.

AI will fundamentally change many things. That is a good thing. Humanity will forever be preserved.

What is Humanity? We will perpetually find out.

Happy Thanksgiving to everyone.

title: Tell HN: Finality is like the speed of light to LLMs from the labs
summary:
I think you've all noticed the "one more thing" with AI, and the many articles to fix it, and that they don't really fix anything at all. If your task ends, so does token spend, so if you ask an LLM to draw a square (metaphor for a moderately complex system), it will forever draw you an approximation of a square, and after stopping it will always tell you that there is still more work to do. Not matter how much you try to force it to finish it just does not. As if physically it can approach but never reach finality.

What has been your experience? Has it improved? How?

summary:
Great launch....bad product? Why did they announce this CVE patch system without it being ready, at all. Borkmann made a lot of really unique(?) choices in his architecture of this programmable ebpf firewall. It feels relatively unusable today, which I guess they said as much in the docs.

Here is a proper version of what they are trying to do. It works right now. Sits on the nic, xdp speed, and you can make the patches yourself if you want. It resets requests carrying the one base64 shape that reaches the bug.

eBPF is the right way to do this, probably the only way realistically. Unsure what Cisco and OpenAI are doing exactly, but the direction is good. Tell me I'm wrong.

title: Tell HN: Lots of Ask HNs again
summary:
There have been questions about why the /ask page (https://news.ycombinator.com/ask) was running dry of Ask HNs - e.g.:

Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984484 - Oct 2026 (47 comments)

Ask HN: Why is pagination gone on "Ask HN", and showing only 19 items? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50280719 - Oct 2026 (3 comments)

I believe I found the problem. The pool of stories for https://news.ycombinator.com/ask has traditionally been drawn from the ranked stories list from which we generate the frontpage. That list is restricted to the top 1500 ranked submissions, and it seems the % of submissions which are text posts (i.e. no linked URL) had declined enough to starve the Ask HN feed. The solution is to compute a separate list of ranked Ask HNs.

p.s. "Ask HN" is the conventional name but it means text posts. The title can also start with "Tell HN" or nothing in particular. They're just posts which were submitted without a URL.

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50649864
